rationale: The 90% claim is deliberately unverified. A statistical chart would lend it false authority; the four evidence-test cards already provide the checking scaffold.
The lesson infers the importance of good character from the hadith. Drawing a literal weighing scale would literalize a religious image rather than teach the intended inference.
The task connects pride, spoken rhythm and declarative style. No complete verse or metric scan is supplied here; a generic desert or poet portrait would not explain those relationships.
The paired terms for separation and companionship already have glosses. A farewell scene would select characters and a setting absent from the supplied passage and would not explain lexical choice.

The modelling already explicitly connects wartime hunger, the night kitchen and the wife sharing bread. A scene would restate the disclosed inference and invent the characters appearance; the bread alone would not teach implicit meaning.
The lamp is a clue to viewpoint, but no specific lamp description or placement is given. An arbitrary lamp photo would turn a textual detail into decoration rather than show who sees it.

The autobiography task asks pupils to locate first person, true events and reflection themselves. No event sequence is supplied for a useful timeline; inventing one would do their comparison for them.
New s6d shows reference and object beams overlapping on a recording plate; explicitly simplified with lenses omitted; scientific basis checked against Georgia State HyperPhysics.
New s6p shows genuine seed-sample containers in Svalbard, labelled as an additional example rather than an assumed location in the reading.

Pupils classify the authors story, statistic and quotation and assess persuasion. No actual items are reproduced here; three generic icons would repeat the named categories without providing evidence.

The listening task evaluates competing arguments, not the literal six qualities. No attributed audio claims are transcribed in the modelling slide; an illustrated list would invent the unheard content.
The ten-step listening topic is used to compare opinions. The deck supplies no actual ten-step sequence, so a flowchart would fabricate the source rather than support listening.

The proverb-presentation task leaves the proverb to the speaker. A preselected proverb scene would narrow that choice; the existing opening-example-conclusion model already teaches delivery structure.
The question about reading as therapy needs an argued oral response. An image of a happy reader would imply the answer instead of helping students support their opinion.
The analytical-essay model already identifies idea, evidence, links and conclusion. An additional sequence would duplicate those explicit writing steps, not add a new relation or concrete source.

Students may choose a writers biography or their own literary experience. A supplied plot arc would choose events for them; the existing beginning-conflict-resolution-ending scaffold preserves that choice.
Five intensive adjective patterns are paired with examples, and alim versus allam is explicitly contrasted. Additional pattern cards would repeat the existing comparison without adding a relation.

The source already pairs morphological patterns with examples and contrasts enduring karim with eventive mukrim. A person illustration could not establish grammatical permanence and would obscure the linguistic evidence.

The earth laughing with flowers is already unpacked as personification with the omitted human and clue identified. A literal smiling earth would encourage a false literal reading; a second text diagram would repeat that analysis.
The synthesis task asks learners to build an idea-evidence-viewpoint table from three sources. Supplying a filled table without those sources would invent positions and remove the synthesis task.
The verse analysis names oath and emphasis particles. A pen photo would not explain the grammatical emphasis, and another labelled verse would merely repeat the existing explanation.
The spring clothing metaphor is already interpreted. A woman-earth composite would literalize the metaphor; the full poem needed for a useful image-to-line comparison is not present.
The lesson compares two literary quotations about the book as a companion. A book-and-person scene would add no evidence beyond the quotations and would fix an interpretation students should discuss.
New s6d shows only the source-deck grounded present scent triggering the grandmother memory; no invented return-to-present plot step.
The cardboard box is an unspecified symbol in very short fiction. A box picture would not teach compression or irony, and a filled plot diagram would disclose a story the deck does not reproduce.

The transformation into a tiger is already described as a symbol of pride. A literal tiger panel would reinforce the surface event, not the authors position; an illustrated transformation would add invented character details.
The central contrast is autobiographical self written as the third-person boy. A portrait would not show narrative distance; the existing explicit pronoun explanation is the relevant scaffold.
The source names UAE innovation examples but asks students to evaluate the article arguments. A building photo would be a proxy for innovation, not evidence for the innovation-or-decline claim.
The distinction is realistic self-worth versus inflated self-worth. Facial expressions cannot establish that mental distinction; the deck gives definitions and asks for two textual proofs.

The creativity listening task compares evidence behind opinions. No specific speaker claims are supplied here, so any illustrated creativity tips would replace rather than support the listening evidence.
The sleep-related listening topic uses an argument-comparison scaffold, with no transcript of its advice. A bedtime sequence would invent advice and would not support comparing speakers.
The spoken poetry analysis assesses voice, organization and evidence. A generic spring landscape would distract from oral analysis and provide no link to the absent full poem.
The future-self presentation intentionally leaves aspirations personal. A chosen profession scene would supply a future identity that is the learners own decision.
The social-media debate needs balanced arguments. Generic phone or smile/frown panels would prejudge benefits and harms without adding sourced evidence.
The innovation essay draws evidence from a named article. A ready-made causal chain would write the argument for learners; the source already provides an essay organization and review checklist.
The two-children writing prompt is open-ended, with no fixed faces or setting. An illustration would constrain the sensory details learners are expected to invent.
The confessions-about-reading task depends on personal recollection. A generic reader image would not teach narrative development and would duplicate the book theme.

The exception types already have separate rule cards and a worked incomplete-negative example. A picture of people cannot encode deletion or syntactic case; another rule tree would repeat those distinctions at this stage.

The specialization construction is explicitly parsed with its omitted verb and contrast to vocative. A group portrait would not identify the hidden grammatical governor; the existing worked sentence carries the distinction.
New s6d aligns two opposite word pairs in the existing example; speaker notes identify excerpts rather than presenting the rearrangement as a full verse.

The introduction asks students to examine linear time, flashback and parallel plots in any novel. No selected event list is supplied for an accurate novel timeline; a filled one would pre-empt the unit reading.
The praise poem is studied through shifts among statement, address and exclamation. A leader portrait would identify the subject but would not show those stylistic changes without the full verses.
The door represents loss and repetition sustains grief. A literal door photograph would privilege the object over the symbolic reading and would not represent the sound pattern.
The biography links pearl-diving hardship to poetry. A generic dhow image would repeat maritime context without showing the textual influence; there is no dated biographical sequence for a timeline.
New s6d separates spoken dialogue above the surface from inferred loneliness and war below, explicitly labelled as a metaphor without measured proportions.
Nature examples are an ant and river, but the inferred lessons are not reproduced. An ant or river panel would repeat nouns rather than show the argument students must retrieve from each paragraph.
Students infer why the author wrote and how writing helped him. The specific experience is not supplied here, so a rescue illustration would invent a literal event and misread the figurative title.
New s6d compares numeral forms and equal value, without any historical chronology or invented dates.
The teacher-replacement statement is a claim to challenge, not a fact. A robot-teacher illustration would legitimize that claim; the deck instead asks for evidence and other sources.

The insomnia listening task contains no reproduced advice or diagnostic content. An illustrated sleep routine would introduce unsupported health recommendations rather than support argument evaluation.
The literature presentation allows any Arab or international writer. A selected author portrait would arbitrarily choose the learners subject and would not teach informed questions and answers.
The essay requires evidence from a biography, sayings and poem about Sheikh Zayed. A portrait would not supply that evidence and would duplicate the named subject rather than the argumentative skill.

The letter addresses a writer chosen for a personal influence. A sample illustrated letter would select an addressee or book not grounded in this prompt; the existing planning checklist preserves the task.
New s6d branches the existing katabtuhu example into verb, subject pronoun and object pronoun, making word segmentation and syntactic role visible.

Fronting the prepositional phrase is already shown with a contrastive worked sentence. A scene cannot encode emphasis, and a second before/after wording panel would repeat the explicit production example.
The opening asks for predictions from the title. A fishing struggle picture would reveal the expected conflict before students form their own prediction.

The Santiago-Manolin relationship is interpreted through loyalty and others judgments. Invented faces or costumes would add ungrounded details; the four source cards already isolate character, relationship and setting.
The departure lesson asks what happens next and why the risk is taken. A scene showing the catch would spoil that prediction, while a generic boat picture would not explain motivation.
External fish conflict, pain and self-doubt are already separate analytical cards. A combat image could show only the external action and would obscure the key internal conflicts.

The present pain and remembered arm-wrestling are already explicitly contrasted. A literal sports image would not explain narrative time; the flashback diagram is being piloted on the simpler thyme example instead of repeating it throughout the unit.
Students are asked what sea, marlin, lions and sharks signify beyond the literal. A picture-to-meaning panel would supply the exact symbolic answers and remove the interpretive step.

The source already gives the catch-attack-resistance-loss sequence. A fully drawn plot curve would supply the climax interpretation pupils are asked to justify, while a shark image would merely repeat the event.
The skeleton and final lion dream are evidence learners interpret. An illustrated ending would foreground the answer and invent visual details, not explain the literary evidence.

The distinction between bodily destruction and undefeated spirit is explicitly explained. A broken body or heroic figure would be both reductive and unsuitable as a literal depiction of the quotation.
The task is to build the novel timeline and place flashbacks. A completed event map would do the assessed organizing work; the existing blank planning instructions preserve that task.

The comparison asks pupils to fill sea, human, conflict and value for Hemingway and Al Jamri. A completed comparison image would supply their textual findings; generic sea photos cannot show individual versus collective experience.
The final project permits diary, letter, critique or film. Illustrating one route would favor that medium; the existing choose-plan-write-review-present sequence supports all options.
